title: From sanctions relief to deterrence: How Iran reads US elections
gist: Iranian officials read the Nov. 2026 US midterms (Democrats win House and Senate) not as a route to sanctions relief but as a political constraint on Washington's willingness to wage war. The purpose of Iranian negotiations has shifted from Rouhani-era economic gains to ending the current US-Israeli conflict and deterring the next one.

themes.theme: Iran's read of the US midterms

insights.claim: Democrats won control of both the US House and Senate in the Nov. 2026 midterm elections, which Iran's speaker and chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf framed as Americans rejecting the war.
insights.speaker: Jamshid Jamshidi
insights.so_what: Divided government may constrain US war-making against Iran, lowering escalation tail risk for oil.
insights.quote: Americans had rejected the war, whether out of conscience or concern about living costs

insights.claim: Ghalibaf warned that Washington would face a 'nightmare' if it ignored the voters' anti-war message, signaling Tehran sees US domestic politics as leverage.
insights.speaker: Jamshid Jamshidi
insights.so_what: Expect Tehran to calibrate pressure to US domestic political costs, e.g. via living-cost/energy price channels.
insights.quote: warned that Washington would face a nightmare if it ignored the voters' message

insights.claim: Iranian leadership interprets the midterm result as a constraint on US willingness to wage war rather than as an opening for improved relations or sanctions relief.
insights.speaker: Jamshid Jamshidi
insights.so_what: Don't price a sanctions-relief trade (more Iranian barrels) off the election result; Tehran itself isn't.
insights.quote: as an opening for improved relations or sanctions relief, but as a constraint on Washington's willingness to wage war

insights.claim: Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi publicly insisted Iran does not tie policy to foreign elections, even as other officials openly timed diplomacy around the US electoral calendar.
insights.speaker: Jamshid Jamshidi
insights.so_what: Official denials of election-timing mask real calendar-driven diplomacy; watch actions not statements.
insights.locator: The previous day, Deputy Foreign Minister

insights.claim: At the September 2026 UN General Assembly, President Masoud Pezeshkian urged Washington to return to a June memorandum of understanding before the midterm vote.
insights.speaker: Jamshid Jamshidi
insights.so_what: An existing June MOU framework is the likely base for any renewed US-Iran deal.
insights.quote: We don't want it to get to the midterm elections.
insights.locator: At the September UN General Assembly

insights.claim: Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, said he saw signs of electoral defeat in Donald Trump's UNGA remarks, showing Tehran's security establishment was betting on a weakened Trump.
insights.speaker: Jamshid Jamshidi
insights.so_what: Tehran's hardliners believe time favors them as Trump's domestic position weakens, reducing urgency to concede.

themes.theme: Shift in what negotiations are for

insights.claim: Under former President Hassan Rouhani, engagement with the US promised sanctions relief, investment and economic development; that economic rationale has now been replaced.
insights.speaker: Jamshid Jamshidi
insights.so_what: The economic-opening trade (Iran investment, oil export normalization) is off the table in Tehran's own framing.
insights.locator: What has changed is the significance

insights.claim: Following the June 2025 Twelve-Day War with Israel and the US-Israeli military campaign that began in February 2026, Iran's negotiators now focus on ending the current conflict and preventing another.
insights.speaker: Jamshid Jamshidi
insights.so_what: An active US-Israeli campaign against Iran since Feb 2026 means negotiations are about war termination—a ceasefire is the key catalyst for Gulf risk premia.
insights.quote: Tehran's negotiators now focus on ending the current conflict and preventing another
insights.locator: What has changed is the significance

insights.claim: Even reformist-era diplomat Javad Zarif now frames diplomacy as part of deterrence rather than economic engagement.
insights.speaker: Jamshid Jamshidi
insights.so_what: Consensus across Iran's factions on diplomacy-as-deterrence suggests a durable, security-first posture.
insights.quote: even Javad Zarif frames diplomacy as part of deterrence
